defects.claim_says: Original section 2(a) reaches persons who obstructed efforts toward a Syria at peace (constitutional process, elections, representative government), adult family members, or expropriation; EO 14312 restates it with 'the three limbs ... kept in changed words, for example without the reference to United Nations supervision of elections'.
defects.source_says: Held EO 13894 section 2(a)(i) has four criteria: (A) obstruction of a ceasefire in northern Syria, (B) intimidation or prevention of displaced persons returning, (C) forcible repatriation, (D) obstruction of a political solution (UN-led constitutional process, UN-supervised elections, new government). EO 14312 section 4(a)(ii) (2025-06-30) replaces 2(a) with only the political-solution criteria; (A)-(C) are struck without replacement. The claim misstates the original clause and omits that cessation, which under the claim's own stated rule (a criterion struck without replacement ends on the striking order's date, applied to 1(a)(i)(B)-(D)) needs a terminated scope or an explained reason.
